# Downside deviation (annualized) (`downside_deviation`)

*Category: Risk summary · Nature: estimated · Unit: decimal_return · Formula id: `downside_deviation@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Variability of returns below the target (0% per period), scaled to a year.

## 2. Formula

```text
sqrt( (1/n) * sum(min(r_t - MAR, 0)^2) ) * sqrt(P), MAR = 0
```

## 3. Required inputs

Periodic simple returns with a regular frequency.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Lower is better.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

How large the losing periods typically are; gains do not count as risk here.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Lower partial moment of order 2 (root), full-sample denominator as in Sortino & Price (1994); the Sortino ratio denominator.

## 7. Assumptions

- Target (MAR) of 0% per period.
- Square-root-of-time scaling.

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- Very few losing periods exist: the estimate rests on a handful of observations.
- Returns are smoothed, which dampens measured losses.

## 9. Minimum sensible data

At least 2 observations; low confidence below 3 years. (policy `dispersion`: Requires at least 2 observations; low confidence below 3 years, moderate below 5.)

## 11. Sources

- Sortino, F. A., & Price, L. N. (1994). Performance Measurement in a Downside Risk Framework. Journal of Investing, 3(3), 59-64.
- Bacon, C. R. (2021). Practical Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement (2nd ed.). Wiley.

## 12. OpenFactsheet convention

MAR = 0; denominator n (all observations), not the number of losing periods (decision 0006).
